questions.q: What three things does a list view filter combine to narrow down records?
options: Object, Record Type, and Owner
Page Layout, Compact Layout, and Related List
Profile, Permission Set, and Role
Field, Operator, and Value
questions.explain: A list view filter is built from a Field, an Operator (equals, contains, greater than, etc.), and a Value — which can itself be relative, like THIS MONTH.

questions.q: Why would an admin use a relative value like "THIS MONTH" instead of a fixed date in a list view filter?
options: Relative values run faster than fixed dates
A relative value keeps a saved filter useful every month, instead of permanently pointing at one fixed date
Fixed dates aren't supported in list view filters at all
Relative values are required for Match All Filters logic
questions.explain: A filter saved with a fixed date becomes stale; a relative value like THIS MONTH keeps the same saved list view relevant indefinitely.

questions.q: What does Salesforce do when a user tries to search a list view's in-list search box for a field that isn't indexed for that search?
options: It silently returns zero results with no explanation
It automatically converts the search into a filter
It shows a tooltip naming the unsearchable fields and suggests using filters or sort instead
It throws an error page and reloads the list view
questions.explain: Salesforce tells the user directly via a tooltip which fields (e.g. Created Date, Unread By Owner) aren't searchable in that list view's search box, and suggests filters or sort instead.

questions.q: How does a Search Layout differ from a list view's own filters?
options: A Search Layout is org-wide, admin-controlled configuration (in Object Manager) of what columns display in search results and lookups, while a list view's filters are per-view and narrow that one saved view
They're the same setting, just named differently in Classic vs. Lightning
A Search Layout only applies to custom objects, never standard ones
A Search Layout controls which users can see a list view at all
questions.explain: Search Layouts, configured per object in Object Manager, set the default columns shown across global search results and lookup dialogs for everyone — distinct from a single list view's own per-view filters.

questions.q: A user can see a field as a column in a list view, but typing it into the list's search box returns nothing. What's the most likely explanation?
options: The list view is broken and needs to be rebuilt
List views only support searching the first column
The user doesn't have field-level security access to that field
That field isn't indexed for in-list search — a filter or sort on that field would work instead
questions.explain: Visible in a list view's columns and searchable via in-list search are two different things — some fields (often system fields) simply aren't indexed for in-list search, which is exactly what Salesforce's own tooltip warns about.
